verdict: Nebius' revenue leapt more than fivefold to $582M as its AI cloud filled up with new GPU capacity — but $5.7B of spending on equipment in a single quarter left it with a $190M loss.

kpis.label: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.note: vs a $21M loss a year ago — the company's own cash-profit measure

kpis.label: Capex (Q2)
kpis.note: Spent on property and equipment in the quarter — building GPU capacity

kpis.label: Operating cash flow
kpis.note: Boosted by customers paying in advance for capacity

segments.name: Nebius AI cloud
segments.note: Renting out GPU computing power (the chips AI runs on) from Nebius's own data centers — the core business. Growth came from adding capacity that filled up fast, at strong prices.

segments.name: TripleTen
segments.note: Online tech bootcamps that retrain people for tech jobs. Sales fell as it moves away from older US courses, partly offset by growth in Latin America.

segments.name: Avride
segments.note: Self-driving cars and delivery robots. Still tiny — just $1M of revenue — and mostly in development.

segments.name: Eliminations
segments.note: Subtracts sales between Nebius's own businesses (for example, other units using the Nebius cloud) so they are not counted twice.

opex.name: Product development
opex.note: Engineers building the AI cloud platform. It includes $84.5M of share-based pay — staff paid in shares rather than cash.

opex.name: Sales, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling, plus running the company — finance, legal and admin.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: The wearing-out cost of servers, GPUs and data centers, spread over their lives. It is huge because Nebius is building capacity so fast.

otherDetail: Everything below operating profit netted to a $0.8M expense: $24.1M of interest income, $81.5M of other income (including foreign-exchange gains) and a $12.7M profit from equity-method stakes such as Toloka, almost exactly offset by $119.1M of interest expense on the company's debt.
footerNote: Nebius had not reported Q3 2026 results as of Nov 7, 2026, so this is its latest reported quarter. Figures are for continuing operations; there were no discontinued-operations results in Q2 2026.
oneTimers: Share-based compensation was $102.5M in the quarter, versus $14.7M a year ago — a real cost of paying staff in shares, and the main reason the company's 'adjusted' net loss of $33.2M looks so much better than the GAAP loss of $190.4M.

The comparison a year ago was flattered the other way: Q2 2025 included a $597.4M gain from revaluing the ClickHouse stake, which turned that quarter's continuing result into a $502.5M profit. There was no such gain this quarter.

takeaways.title: The AI cloud exploded
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 454% to $582.3M. The AI cloud alone brought in $574.9M, up 514%, as Nebius added GPU capacity and filled it at strong prices and high utilization. The other businesses are now rounding errors by comparison.

takeaways.title: Cash-profitable before the build-out costs
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA swung to a $236.2M profit from a $21.0M loss a year ago. The loss appears lower down: $259.7M of depreciation on all the new servers and data centers, and $119.1M of interest, turned the quarter to a $190.4M net loss.

takeaways.title: Spending at full speed
takeaways.text: Nebius spent $5,657.4M on property and equipment in this one quarter. Customers paying in advance helped operating cash flow reach $2,246.1M, and the company has since added a $3.5B credit facility (October 2026) to keep funding the build-out.

sources.label: Interim report with segment detail (SEC EDGAR 6-K Ex-99.1)
